old: पुरस्कार की कामना करने वाले के समान अब अग्नि के रथों की, योगों (जुती हुई टोलियों) की स्तुति करो, जो अत्यन्त यशस्वी और उदार हैं।
new: पुरस्कार की कामना करने वाले के समान अब रथों की, टोलियों की स्तुति करो, अत्यन्त यशस्वी, उदार अग्नि के।
why: reviewer (minor): Bracketed gloss in Hindi (not allowed); also the relative clause "जो ... हैं" attaches to the chariots/teams, whereas yaśastamasya mīḻhuṣaḥ are genitives agreeing with agneḥ (as English and the note say).

old: He who is a good leader to the giver, unageing, making the foe grow old, fair-faced, offered to.
new: He who is a good leader to the giver, unageing, making the foe grow old, fair-faced, to whom offering is made.
why: reviewer (minor): "offered to" is not a complete rendering of āhutaḥ (ā-√hu, ppp.).

old: āhutaḥ could also be rendered 'invoked'. arim: 'foe' (ari, also 'stranger'); jarayan is the causative of √jṝ, 'making decay'. The relative yaḥ continues the sentence of verse 1 (Agni).
new: āhutaḥ (short u) is from ā-√hu 'pour in, offer'; 'invoked' would need āhūtaḥ. arim: 'foe' (ari, also 'stranger'); jarayan is the causative of √jṝ, 'making decay'. The relative yaḥ continues the sentence of verse 1 (Agni).
why: reviewer (minor): The printed vowel is short (āhutaḥ, ā-√hu); "invoked" belongs to āhūta (ā-√hve) with a long ū, which is not the printed form.
reviewer (minor): dama (house) is masculine in the Ṛgveda, not neuter.

old: जो सूर्य के समान अपनी किरण से प्रकट होकर चमकता है, विचित्र (तेजस्वी), ज्वाला से, अजर (शिखाओं) को सजाता हुआ।
new: जो स्वर्ग के प्रकाश के समान तेज से प्रकट होकर चमकता है, उज्ज्वल, ज्वाला से, अजरों से सजता हुआ।
why: reviewer (error): Two bracketed interpretations in the Hindi; "अजर (शिखाओं) को" is accusative while ajaraiḥ is instrumental (English has "with"); "अपनी किरण" and "सूर्य" do not follow the glossary or add "अपनी".

old: Who shines forth like the sun with his light, bright, with his flame, adorning with the unageing ones.
new: Who shines forth like heaven's light with radiance, bright, with flame, adorning with the unageing ones.
why: reviewer (minor): Glossary: svar = (heaven's) light, not "sun"; "his" is not in the text.
reviewer (minor): Align with the English "with radiance".

old: Like Atri, now, the hymns have strengthened Agni, the sovereign rule. He has taken on all splendours.
new: After Atri, the hymns have strengthened Agni, the sovereign rule. He has taken on all splendours.

old: अत्रि के समान अब स्वराज्य, अग्नि को स्तोत्रों ने बढ़ाया है। उसने सब शोभाएँ धारण की हैं।
new: अत्रि के पीछे स्वराज्य, अग्नि को स्तोत्रों ने बढ़ाया है। उसने सब शोभाएँ धारण की हैं।

old: The first token is doubtful and the reading 'like Atri, now' is tentative. svarājyam: taken as a noun 'sovereignty, self-rule' in apposition to agnim; the construction is uncertain. viśvāḥ adhi śriyaḥ dadhe: 'he has set (taken) all splendours upon himself'; the subject is Agni, not stated.
new: atrim anu: 'after Atri' (anu with the accusative atrim); the printed text is sound, and the sense of the phrase is still tentative. svarājyam: taken as a noun 'sovereignty, self-rule' in apposition to agnim; the construction is uncertain. viśvāḥ adhi śriyaḥ dadhe: 'he has set (taken) all splendours upon himself'; the subject is Agni, not stated.
why: reviewer (minor): Note repeats the wrong reading.

new: m. nom. pl. fut. part. a-√riṣ
why: reviewer (minor): ariṣyant is the future participle (a-√riṣ, "not about to be harmed"), not a present participle.
